What is light energy?

Great question! Light is a form of energy that helps us to see things around us. Without light, everything would be dark, like when NEPA takes the power at night and the whole room goes black. Light energy comes from different sources. The sun is our biggest natural source of light. Other sources include electric bulbs, torches, candles, kerosene lamps and even fireflies that glow at night. When light from any of these falls on objects, it bounces into our eyes and we see. Light is a gift we use every single day. Keep observing the world!

What are natural and artificial sources of light?

Well done for asking! Sources of light are divided into two groups. Natural sources are made by nature, not by people. The best example is the sun; others are the stars, lightning during a rainstorm, and fireflies that glow at night. Artificial sources are made by human beings. Examples are electric bulbs, torches, phone flashlights, candles, kerosene lanterns and generators powering our lights. Here is an easy check: if nobody manufactured it, it is natural; if it was made or built by people, it is artificial. Look around tonight and name each light you see. Great work!

How does light travel?

Good question! Light travels in straight lines. It does not bend around corners by itself. You can see this when sunlight enters a dark room through a small hole in the roof; the beam looks like a straight rod of light. A torch also throws its light straight ahead. This is why you cannot see around a wall: the light from things behind the wall cannot bend to reach your eyes. Because light travels straight, objects in its path block it and form shadows. Try making a straight beam with a torch in a dark room. Science is fun!

What is a shadow and how is it formed?

Lovely question! A shadow is the dark shape that forms when an object blocks light. Remember, light travels in straight lines, so when something solid stands in its way, the light cannot pass through, and a dark patch appears behind the object. That dark patch is the shadow, and it takes the shape of the object. Stand outside in the morning sun and you will see your own long shadow on the ground. At midday, when the sun is overhead, your shadow becomes short. Play a shadow game with a friend and watch how shadows change. Enjoy!

Why can I see through glass but not through wood?

Sharp observation! Materials behave differently with light. Transparent materials, like clear glass and clean water, allow light to pass through completely, so you can see through them clearly. Translucent materials allow only some light to pass, so you see a blurry picture; examples are frosted glass and thin nylon. Opaque materials do not allow light to pass at all, so you cannot see through them; examples are wood, stone, metal and your own body. That is why a wooden door blocks your view but a glass window does not. Look for examples of all three at home!

What are the uses of light in our daily lives?

Great question! We use light in many ways every day. Light helps us see, so we can read, write, cook, play and walk safely at night. Sunlight helps plants make their own food, and those plants feed people and animals. Sunlight also helps our bodies stay strong and dries our washed clothes and grains like maize. Drivers use headlights at night, and traffic lights guide cars safely. Doctors use special lights to examine patients. Solar panels even turn sunlight into electricity for homes and street lights in many Nigerian towns. Light truly powers our daily lives!

Why does my spoon look bent inside a glass of water?

What a wonderful observation! Your spoon is not really bent. This trick of light is called refraction. Light bends slightly when it moves from one substance to another, like from air into water. The light coming from the part of the spoon inside the water bends as it leaves the water, so your eyes are deceived, and the spoon looks broken or bent at the water line. Lift the spoon out and it is perfectly straight again! Refraction also makes a swimming pool or a bucket of water look shallower than it really is. Keep asking curious questions!

How can I protect my eyes from strong light?

Very important question! Our eyes are precious, so we must protect them. Never look directly at the sun, not even during an eclipse, because its strong light can damage your eyes forever. Do not stare at welding sparks by the roadside; welders wear special dark masks for a reason. Avoid shining torches or laser lights into anyone's eyes, including your own. When reading, use enough light, but not harsh light that strains your eyes, and do not hold your phone or book too close to your face for long. If your eyes hurt or you cannot see the board clearly, tell an adult. Guard your eyes well!
